paragraphs.title: Elisha’s Prophecy and the Officer’s Doubt

answers: The king
Elisha
The lepers
easy.explanation: Elisha said, “Hear ye the word of the LORD,” and proclaimed the coming abundance.
easy.q: Who declared the prophecy about abundant grain in Samaria?

answers: Chariots and horses
Fine flour and barley
Gold and silver
easy.explanation: A measure of fine flour and two measures of barley were to be sold for a shekel.
easy.q: What was to be sold in the gate of Samaria the next day?

answers: He doubted that it could happen
He immediately believed it
He went to the Syrian camp
easy.explanation: The officer asked, “If the LORD would make windows in heaven, might this thing be?”
easy.q: How did the officer respond to Elisha’s prophecy?

answers: He would see the abundance but not eat it
He would eat the first grain sold
He would flee from Samaria
medium.explanation: Elisha told him, “Thou shalt see it with thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof.”
medium.q: What would happen to the officer according to Elisha?

answers: He was punished for leaving the city
He was punished because he did not believe the prophecy
He was punished for taking Syrian goods
medium.explanation: Because he doubted the LORD’s word through Elisha, he would see the fulfillment but not benefit from it.
medium.q: What connection does the passage show between the officer’s doubt and his punishment?

answers: A quantity used to measure grain
A city gate
A military command
medium.explanation: A measure was a stated quantity of grain, not a place or a military term.
medium.q: In the phrase “a measure of fine flour,” what does “measure” refer to?

answers: A change from famine and siege to abundant food
A change from peace to war
A change from abundance to famine
challenge.explanation: The low prices of flour and barley show that the famine would be replaced by abundance.
challenge.q: What major change in Samaria is announced by the prophecy?

answers: It would happen by the next day
It would happen after many years
It would happen only after another war
challenge.explanation: The prophecy says, “To morrow about this time,” showing that the fulfillment would be immediate.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes how quickly the change would occur?

answers: Elisha speaks the LORD’s word, while the officer relies on doubt
Elisha wants to flee, while the officer wants to fight
Elisha gathers wealth, while the officer gives it away
challenge.explanation: Elisha announces God’s word, while the officer questions whether it can come to pass.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast between Elisha and the officer?

paragraphs.title: The Lepers Discover the Abandoned Camp

answers: Two
Four
Five
easy.explanation: The passage says, “There were four leprous men at the entering in of the gate.”
easy.q: How many leprous men were sitting at the gate?

answers: Unto the camp of the Syrians
Into the king’s house
To another city gate
easy.explanation: They decided to go to the Syrian camp because remaining where they were meant certain death.
easy.q: Where did the lepers decide to go?

answers: The camp was full of soldiers
There was no man there
The city gates were open
easy.explanation: At the uttermost part of the camp, they saw that there was no man there.
easy.q: What did the lepers discover when they reached the camp?

answers: Death awaited them wherever else they went
They wanted to speak with the king of Syria
The king of Israel had sent them
medium.explanation: They reasoned that they would die in the city or by remaining where they were, so they chose to risk going to the Syrians.
medium.q: Why did the lepers decide to go to the Syrian camp?

answers: They heard the noise of chariots, horses, and a great host
The lepers attacked them
The king of Israel entered the camp
medium.explanation: The LORD caused the Syrians to hear the sound of a great army, so they believed help was coming against them.
medium.q: What caused the Syrians to flee?

answers: At dusk or as darkness began
At midday
Inside the city
medium.explanation: The lepers rose in the twilight, the dim time between daylight and night.
medium.q: What does “in the twilight” mean in this passage?

answers: They ate and drank, took goods, and hid them
They reported to the king, then ate and fled
They fought the Syrians and returned with horses
challenge.explanation: They entered one tent, ate and drank, carried away valuables, and hid them before entering another tent.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes what the lepers did in the camp?

answers: The Syrians fled in great haste
The Syrians planned to remain there
The camp had always been empty
challenge.explanation: Leaving the camp and its animals behind indicates a sudden and hurried flight.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the tents, horses, and asses being left behind?

answers: They made the Syrians believe that a great army was approaching
They told the lepers that the city was open
They caused the king of Israel to leave the city
challenge.explanation: The Syrians interpreted the sounds as armies hired by Israel coming against them.
challenge.q: Why were the sounds of an army significant even though no army was actually seen?

answers: They needed to fight
It was wrong to keep silent about the news
They needed to remain in the camp
easy.explanation: They said, “This day is a day of good tidings, and we hold our peace.”
easy.q: What did the lepers realize after eating and taking goods?

answers: The porter of the city
The kings of Egypt
The Syrians
easy.explanation: They came and called unto the porter of the city.
easy.q: To whom did the lepers report the empty camp?

answers: The lepers themselves
The porters
The Syrians
easy.explanation: The porters told the news to the king’s house within.
easy.q: Who carried the report into the king’s house?

answers: The city needed to hear about the deliverance
The king had commanded them to leave
They were afraid of the horses
medium.explanation: They feared that if they waited until morning, some mischief would come upon them.
medium.q: Why did the lepers consider delaying the news to be wrong?

answers: The Syrian camp was empty of people
The king had gone to war
The city had been burned
medium.explanation: They reported that there was no man in the camp, only tied horses and asses and standing tents.
medium.q: What news did the lepers report?

answers: A day when good news should be announced
A day of fasting
A day when the people went to battle
medium.explanation: The lepers had discovered news that could bring relief to the starving city.
medium.q: What does “a day of good tidings” mean in this context?

answers: They move from personal enjoyment to responsibility toward the city
They move from fear of the city to attacking the Syrians
They move from reporting the news to hiding from everyone
challenge.explanation: They first ate and gathered goods for themselves, but then recognized their duty to tell the city.
challenge.q: What is the main change in the lepers’ behavior?

answers: The lepers called to them, and they carried the report to the king’s house
The porters discovered the camp themselves
The porters were leaders of Syria
challenge.explanation: This is the sequence explicitly described in the passage.
challenge.q: Why did the news pass through the city porters?

answers: Tied horses and asses and standing tents were found there
A great army was found in the camp
The gates of Samaria were already open
challenge.explanation: The remaining animals and tents showed that the Syrians had truly fled and left the camp behind.
challenge.q: Which detail supports the truth of the report about the abandoned camp?

paragraphs.title: The King’s Suspicion and the Investigation

answers: An ambush by the Syrians
Famine in the Syrian camp
That the lepers would become kings
easy.explanation: The king suspected that the Syrians had hidden themselves in the field to capture the Israelites.

answers: Sending men to investigate the camp
Closing the city gate
Bringing the Syrians back
easy.explanation: The servant proposed taking some of the remaining horses and sending men to see.
easy.q: What did one of the king’s servants suggest?

answers: Unto Jordan
Unto Egypt
Only to the gate of Samaria
easy.explanation: They followed the Syrians unto Jordan.
easy.q: How far did the messengers follow the Syrians’ path?

answers: To test the report without risking the whole population
To attack the Syrian camp
To flee from the city
medium.explanation: He proposed a limited investigation using only a few horses and messengers.
medium.q: Why did the servant suggest using the remaining horses?

answers: Garments and vessels cast away by the Syrians
A Syrian army ready for battle
Food sent by the king
medium.explanation: The road to Jordan was full of garments and vessels that the Syrians had abandoned.
medium.q: What did the riders find along the way?

answers: In their speed and panic
Quietly and in good order
While sitting for a long time
medium.explanation: The Syrians cast away their belongings while fleeing quickly.

answers: The servant’s proposal to send riders
The arrival of a new army
A command from Syria
challenge.explanation: The servant suggested a limited test, and the king accepted it.
challenge.q: What caused the king to move from suspicion to practical investigation?

answers: Much property had been thrown along the road
The gates of Samaria were closed
The lepers had disappeared
challenge.explanation: The garments and vessels scattered all the way to Jordan showed that the Syrians had fled in haste.
challenge.q: Which detail strengthened the possibility that the Syrian camp had truly been abandoned?

answers: The king suspects an ambush, the servant proposes an investigation, riders are sent, and goods are found
Goods are found, the king suspects an ambush, the servant proposes an investigation, and riders are sent
Riders are sent, the servant proposes an investigation, the king suspects an ambush, and goods are found
challenge.explanation: This is the order in which the events occur in verses 12–15.

paragraphs.title: The Prophecy of Abundance Is Fulfilled

answers: They spoiled it
They burned the city
They returned it to Syria
easy.explanation: The people went out and spoiled the tents of the Syrians.
easy.q: What did the people do to the Syrian camp?

answers: They became exactly as Elisha had prophesied
They rose greatly
Grain could not be purchased
easy.explanation: Fine flour and barley were sold for the prices Elisha had announced.
easy.q: What happened to the prices of the grain?

answers: He became king
He was trodden upon and died at the gate
He ate from the abundant grain
easy.explanation: The people trode upon him in the gate, and he died.

answers: There was abundant grain at the prices he had named
The officer ate from the abundance
The Syrians returned to the city
medium.explanation: The prices in Samaria were exactly those announced by Elisha.

answers: He saw the grain but did not eat it
He fled before the abundance arrived
He received the Syrian camp
medium.explanation: He was placed at the gate, saw the abundance, and was trampled before he could benefit from it.
medium.q: How was the officer’s punishment fulfilled?

answers: They stepped on him as they passed
They crowned him
They sent him to the Syrian camp
medium.explanation: The people trampled him underfoot at the gate, causing his death.
medium.q: What does “the people trode upon him” mean?

answers: The abundance of grain and the officer’s punishment
The return of Syria and the rise of prices
The lepers’ flight and the king’s death
challenge.explanation: Both the promised grain prices and the officer’s death occurred as Elisha had said.
challenge.q: Which two things were fulfilled at the end of the chapter?

answers: The prophecy concerned the gate, and its fulfillment was seen there
The Syrian army gathered there
The lepers hid there
challenge.explanation: Elisha announced the prices at the gate, and the abundance appeared there the next day.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the gate of Samaria at the beginning and end of the chapter?

answers: The story presents the prophecy as true and fulfilled
The story proves that the officer was correct
The story shows that the camp was not abandoned
challenge.explanation: The fulfillment of both the abundance and the officer’s judgment confirms the truth of Elisha’s word.
challenge.q: What does the officer’s death show about Elisha’s prophecy?
